data.narrative:
Heaviside is a Series A defense and security company founded by Phillip Walker that has raised $28M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 11 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies: 2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms including Anduril Industries, Helsing, NODA AI, Singularity, and Castelion.

The stage-progression method was inapplicable; its implied $1.2B valuation exceeded 20x total capital raised, indicating an unreliable base value. Instead, peer-median triangulation anchored the analysis. The 11-company peer set (spanning $125M–$3.0B) yielded a median valuation of $1.0B. Sample peers at Series B stage include Dream Security at $3.0B, Allen Control Systems at $2.2B, Harmattan AI at $1.4B, Code Metal at $1.2B, and Twenty at $1.0B.

The analysis supports a range of $850M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median point estimate of $1.0B. This valuation reflects peer-comparable multiples in the defense-tech sector at Heaviside's stage and capital deployment. Key uncertainties include customer concentration, technology differentiation relative to the peer set, and the Defense & Security sector's exposure to budget and policy cycles. The single-method basis underscores the importance of near-term revenue traction in narrowing the range.
